note: Editor Advanced Image is a CKEditor 5 plugin (Drupal plugin id editor_advanced_image_image, JS plugin editorAdvancedImage.EditorAdvancedImage). It has no configure route (configure=null), no admin page, no permissions, no Drush, and defines no plugin types. Its only persistent state is per-text-format config inside editor.editor.<format> at settings.plugins.editor_advanced_image_image with keys disable_balloon (bool), default_class (string), enabled_attributes (sequence of title/class/id; default ['class']). Medium/hard cases are grounded in that real config using dedicated CKEditor5 formats (eai_known/eai_hidden/eai_task/eai_dbtask) created and torn down by the scripts so no shared format is touched.

evals.prompt: In Drupal, the editor_advanced_image (Editor Advanced Image) CKEditor 5 module lets authors edit image attributes from the image balloon. Which HTML attributes on an can it let editors set?
evals.expected_output: It supports exactly three attributes: title, class, and id (SUPPORTED_ATTRIBUTES). An administrator allowlists which of them appear via the enabled_attributes setting per text format.

evals.prompt: The editor_advanced_image module has no admin settings page and no configure route. On a Drupal 11 site, where do I configure it and where are its settings stored in config?
evals.expected_output: You configure it per text format on the CKEditor 5 configuration form (/admin/config/content/formats). Settings are stored inside that format's editor.editor.<format> config entity at settings.plugins.editor_advanced_image_image (disable_balloon, default_class, enabled_attributes).

evals.prompt: What does the 'Default image class(es)' (default_class) setting of editor_advanced_image do, and what is the 'Disable Balloon' (disable_balloon) setting for?
evals.expected_output: default_class is a space-separated list of CSS classes automatically added to newly inserted inline images (e.g. img-fluid). disable_balloon, when true, hides the Editor Advanced Image balloon/form button entirely so authors cannot edit the attributes.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a CKEditor 5 text format with machine name 'eai_known' that uses the Editor Advanced Image plugin. Inspect the live editor configuration for that format and tell me the value of its 'default image class(es)' (default_class) setting.
evals.expected_output: default_class is 'teaser-img'. In editor.editor.eai_known, settings.plugins.editor_advanced_image_image has default_class: teaser-img and enabled_attributes [class, title].

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a CKEditor 5 text format 'eai_hidden' using Editor Advanced Image. Inspect its live configuration: is the Editor Advanced Image balloon button enabled or disabled on that format?
evals.expected_output: The balloon is disabled: in editor.editor.eai_hidden, settings.plugins.editor_advanced_image_image has disable_balloon: true, so the Editor Advanced Image button is hidden on that format.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a CKEditor 5 text format with machine name 'eai_task' that already uses the Editor Advanced Image plugin. Using that module, configure the format so authors can set BOTH the image 'title' and 'id' attributes (in addition to class), and make every newly inserted image get the default class 'img-fluid'. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In editor.editor.eai_task, settings.plugins.editor_advanced_image_image.enabled_attributes must include title and id, and default_class must be 'img-fluid' (e.g. load the Editor entity, merge the plugin settings, save).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a CKEditor 5 text format with machine name 'eai_dbtask' using Editor Advanced Image. We want to turn OFF the Editor Advanced Image balloon button on this format so authors can no longer edit image attributes there, without removing the plugin. Apply the change to the live default configuration.
evals.expected_output: In editor.editor.eai_dbtask, settings.plugins.editor_advanced_image_image.disable_balloon must be set to true.
